entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Euryale changes shape into her Huge serpent form or back into her Medium medusa form. Euryale's game statistics are the same in each form except where noted in this stat block. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. Euryale reverts to her medusa form if she dies.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Euryale unleashes petrifying magic from her eyes in a cone (Close range). Each creature in that area must make a Strength Reaction Roll if it doesn't have the blinded condition. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the creature has the petrified condition. Otherwise, on a failure, the creature takes 4d6 magic damage, begins to turn to stone, and has the restrained condition. The restrained creature must repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of its next turn. On a failure, it has the petrified condition, and on a successful Reaction Roll, the effect ends on it, The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the Greater Restoration spell or other magic A creature can use its reaction, if available, to shut its eyes to avoid the Reaction Roll. If the creature does so, it has the blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

The evoker can select up to three creatures it can see in the area to ignore the spell, as the evoker sculpts the spell's energy around them. On a failure, a creature takes 9d8 damage of the chosen type and is knocked prone (Vulnerable). On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone (Vulnerable).

entries.name: Antimagic Gullet
entries.description: Action: Magical effects, including those produced by spells and magic items but excluding those created by artifacts or deities, are suppressed inside the eye monger's gullet. Any spell slot or charge expended by a creature in the gullet to cast a spell or activate a property of a magic item is wasted. While an effect is suppressed, it doesn't function, but the time it spends suppressed counts against its duration. No spell or magical effect that originates outside the eye monger's gullet, except one created by an artifact or a deity, can affect a creature or an object inside the gullet.

entries.name: False Appearance
entries.description: Passive: If the eye monger is motionless and has its eye and mouth closed at the start of combat, it has advantage on its initiative roll. Moreover, if a creature hasn't observed the eye monger move or act, that creature must succeed on a Knowledge Roll (18) to discern that the eye monger is animate.

entries.name: Unusual Nature
entries.description: Passive: The eye monger doesn't require air.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 2d6+5 physical damage plus 10d6 magic damage (acid). If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or be swallowed by the eye monger and deposited in the eye monger's gullet (see Antimagic Gullet). The eye monger can swallow one creature at a time. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and other effects originating outside the eye monger, and takes at the start of each of its turns. If the eye monger takes 25 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside its gullet, the eye monger regurgitates the swallowed creature, which falls prone (Vulnerable) in a space within Very Close range of the eye monger. If the eye monger dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using Very Close range of movement, exiting prone.

Each creature in that area must make a Strength Reaction Roll, taking 6d12 magic damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a successful one. Every spell of 3rd level or lower ends on creatures and objects of the eyedrake's choice in that area.

entries.name: Eye Rays
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The eyedrake shoots three of the following magical eye rays at random (reroll duplicates), each ray targeting one creature it can see within Far range of it:1: Freezing Ray. The target must make a Strength Reaction Roll. On a failure, the target takes 5d6 magic damage (cold), and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn. On a successful Reaction Roll, the target takes half as much damage with no additional effects.2: Debilitating Ray. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or take 2d6 magic damage (thunder) and become incapacitated until the end of its next turn.3: Repulsion Ray. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or take 4d6 magic damage and be pushed up to Far range away from the eyedrake.4: Fire Ray. The target must make an Agility Reaction Roll, taking 6d6 magic damage (fire) on a failure, or half as much damage on a successful one.5: Paralyzing Ray. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.6: Death Ray. The target must make an Agility Reaction Roll, taking 8d6 magic damage (necrotic) on a failure, or half as much damage on a successful one. The target dies if the ray reduces it to 0 HP.

If the eyestalk dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using Close range of movement, exiting prone.

Crushing a gem releases any souls trapped within, at which point the soul's body re-forms in an unoccupied space nearest to the gem and in the same state as it was when its soul was trapped.

entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Each non-undead creature within Far range of Fidelio that can see it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that Fidelio can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by Fidelio; Fidelio then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. Fidelio now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. Fidelio can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, Fidelio ends it or Fidelio is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, Fidelio reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Berserk
entries.description: Passive: Whenever the golem starts its turn with 100 HP or fewer, roll a d6. On a 6, the golem goes berserk. On each of its turns while berserk, the golem attacks the nearest creature it can see. If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its HP. If the golem's creator is within Far range of the berserk golem, the creator can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a Presence Roll (15). If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at 100 HP or fewer, the golem might go berserk again.

The rock restraining each creature has Difficulty 17; 20 HP; and immunity to fire, poison, and psychic damage. On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage only.

On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage. At the same time as the colossus releases this exhalation, creatures inside the colossus's chest cavity take 9d8 magic damage from churning elemental energy.

A swallowed creature has the restrained condition, has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the colossus, and takes at the start of each of the colossus's turns. The colossus's chest cavity can hold up to two creatures at a time. Inside its chest cavity is its core, which is a Large object with Difficulty 16 that is immune to lightning, poison, and psychic damage. It has 140 HP and sheds dim light in a radius (Very Close range). If the core is destroyed, the colossus regurgitates all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in a space within Very Close range of the colossus and is knocked prone (Vulnerable), and the colossus can no longer swallow a creature. If the colossus dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using Very Close range of movement, exiting with the prone condition.

entries.description: Reaction: When a creature that can see the gauth's central eye starts its turn within Close range of the gauth, the gauth can force it to make an Instinct Reaction Roll if the gauth isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. A creature that fails the Reaction Roll is stunned until the start of its next turn. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes at the start of its turn to avoid the Reaction Roll. If the creature does so, it can't see the gauth until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the gauth in the meantime, it must immediately make the Reaction Roll.

The target must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or have one of its magic items lose all magical properties until the start of the gauth's next turn. If the object is a charged item, it also loses 1d4 charges. Determine the affected item randomly, ignoring single-use items such as potions and scrolls.2: Enervation Ray. The target must make a Strength Reaction Roll, taking 4d8 magic damage (necrotic) on a failure, or half as much damage on a successful one.3: Fire Ray. The target must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 4d10 magic damage (fire).4: Paralyzing Ray. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be paralyzed for 1 minute. The target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.5: Pushing Ray. The target must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be pushed up to Close range away from the gauth and have its speed halved until the start of the gauth's next turn.6: Sleep Ray. The target must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or fall asleep and remain unconscious for 1 minute. The target awakens if it takes damage or another creature takes an action to wake it. This ray has no effect on Constructs and Undead.

If the target is a creature that is Medium or smaller, it must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be moved up to Close range directly away from the gazer. If the target is a Tiny object that isn't being worn or carried, the gazer moves it up to Close range in any direction. The gazer can also exert fine control on objects with this ray, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a container.

Other creatures can enter that space, but a creature that does so is subjected to the cube's Engulf and has Disadvantage on the Reaction Roll. Creatures inside the cube have Total Cover, and the cube can hold one Large creature or up to four Medium or Small creatures inside itself at a time. As an action, a creature within Melee range of the cube can pull a creature or an object out of the cube by succeeding on a Strength Roll (12), and the puller takes 3d6 magic damage (acid).

The cube can move through the spaces of Large or smaller creatures if it has room inside itself to contain them (see the Ooze Cube trait). Each creature whose space the cube enters for the first time during this move must make an Agility Reaction Roll. Targets who fail take 3d6 magic damage (acid), and the target is engulfed. An engulfed target is suffocating, can't cast spells with a Verbal component, has the Restrained condition, and takes 3d6 magic damage (acid) at the start of each of the cube's turns. When the cube moves, the engulfed target moves with it. An engulfed target can try to escape by taking an action to make a Strength Roll (12). On a successful check, the target escapes and enters the nearest unoccupied space. Targets who succeed take half damage., and the target moves to an unoccupied space within Melee range of the cube. If there is no unoccupied space, the target fails the Reaction Roll instead.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The gingwatzim changes from its true form—a Melee-diameter sphere of luminous ectoplasm—into one of its two alternate forms, or from one of those forms back into its true form. In object form, it can't move or make attacks but otherwise retains its statistics, and it is indistinguishable from the thing it is imitating. In beast form, it retains its HP but otherwise uses the stat block of the beast it is imitating. When it dies, the gingwatzim reverts to its true form and then vanishes.

entries.name: Engulf
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Glabbagool moves up to its speed. While doing so, it can enter Large or smaller creatures' spaces. Whenever Glabbagool enters a creature's space, the creature must make an Agility Reaction Roll. On a successful Reaction Roll, the creature can choose to be pushed Melee range back or to the side of Glabbagool. A creature that chooses not to be pushed suffers the consequences of a failed Reaction Roll. On a failure, Glabbagool enters the creature's space, and the creature takes 3d6 magic damage (acid) and is engulfed. The engulfed creature can't breathe, is restrained, and takes 6d6 magic damage (acid) at the start of each of Glabbagool's turns. When Glabbagool moves, the engulfed creature moves with it. An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a Strength Roll (12). On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within Melee range of Glabbagool.

entries.name: Shapechanger
entries.description: Passive: If the vampire isn't in sunlight, it can use its action to polymorph into a Large hyena or a Medium cloud of mist, or back into its true form. While in hyena form, the vampire can't speak, and its walking speed is Far range. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are unchanged. Anything it is wearing transforms with it, but nothing it is carrying does. It reverts to its true form if it dies. While in mist form, the vampire can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of Close range, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, and it can't pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Strength Reaction Rolls, and it is immune to all non-magical damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight.

If it hears words of Celestial spoken, the vampire must try to attack the source of those spoken words on its next turn. If these words come from multiple sources and from opposite directions, the vampire is restrained. Otherwise, it moves to attack what it perceives to be the closest source. Repulsed by Perfume. The vampire has disadvantage on melee attacks made against any creature wearing perfume or carrying an open container of it. Stake to the Heart. If a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into the vampire's heart while the vampire is incapacitated in its resting place, the vampire is paralyzed until the stake is removed. Sunlight Hypersensitivity. The vampire takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.

On a second failure: The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition.

entries.name: Rotting Fist
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 3d6+4 physical damage plus 6d6 magic damage (necrotic). If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be cursed with mummy rot. The cursed target can't regain HP, and its HP maximum decreases by 3d6 for every 24 hours that elapse. If the curse reduces the target's HP maximum to 0, the target dies, and its body turns to dust. The curse lasts until removed by the remove curse spell or other magic.

entries.name: Dreadful Glare
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The mummy lord targets one creature it can see within Far range of it. If the target can see the mummy lord, it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll against this magic or become frightened until the end of the mummy's next turn. If the target fails the Reaction Roll by 5 or more, it is also paralyzed for the same duration. A target that succeeds on the Reaction Roll is immune to the Dreadful Glare of all mummies and mummy lords for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Enlarge
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. For 1 minute, the mummy lord magically increases in size, along with anything it is wearing or carrying. While enlarged, the mummy lord is Large, doubles its damage dice with its Rotting Fist attack, and makes Strength checks and Strength Reaction Rolls with advantage. If the mummy lord lacks the room to become Large, it attains the maximum size possible in the space available.

entries.name: Invisibility
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mummy lord magically turns invisible for up to 1 hour or until it attacks, it casts a spell, it uses its Enlarge, or its concentration is broken (as if concentrating on a spell). Any equipment the mummy lord wears or carries is invisible with it. The stalagmite in the northwest alcove is hollow and serves as Gorka Tharn's sarcophagus. The mummy lord is lodged inside the stalagmite's funnel-shaped interior. When it awakens, the mummy lord uses a stone shape spell to create an opening large enough for it to emerge. It destroys any intruders in its lair, then returns to its sarcophagus and its slumber. At the bottom of the stalagmite's hollow cavity, four Melee-tall clay urns contain Gorka Tharn's preserved internal organs, including the mummy lord's shriveled heart. Only by destroying the heart can the characters prevent the mummy lord from rejuvenating. The heart is a Tiny object with Difficulty 5, 25 HP, and immunity to all damage except fire.

entries.name: Attack
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mummy lord makes one attack with its rotting fist or uses its Dreadful Glare.

entries.name: Blinding Dust
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Blinding dust and sand swirls magically around the mummy lord. Each creature within Melee range of the mummy lord must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be blinded until the end of the creature's next turn.

entries.name: Blasphemous Word
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mummy lord utters a blasphemous word. Each non-undead creature within Very Close range of the mummy lord that can hear the magical utterance must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be stunned until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.

entries.name: Channel Negative Energy
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mummy lord magically unleashes negative energy. Creatures within Far range of the mummy lord, including ones behind barriers and around corners, can't regain HP until the end of the mummy lord's next turn.

entries.name: Whirlwind of Sand
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mummy lord magically transforms into a whirlwind of sand, moves up to Far range, and reverts to its normal form. While in whirlwind form, the mummy lord is immune to all damage, and it can't be grappled, petrified, knocked prone (Vulnerable), restrained, or stunned. Equipment worn or carried by the mummy lord remain in its possession.

Whenever Grandlejaw takes 25 or more damage in a single turn, one of its heads dies. If all its heads die, Grandlejaw dies. At the end of its turn, it grows two heads for each of its heads that died since its last turn, unless it has taken fire damage since its last turn. Grandlejaw regains 10 HP for each head regrown in this way.

The revenant can have up to two targets Grappled in this way at a time.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One Humanoid Gremorly can see within Melee range of himself must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by him; Gremorly disappears, and the target has the incapacitated condition and loses control of its body. Gremorly can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn Undead, and he retains his alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to the charmed and frightened conditions. He otherwise uses the target's game statistics, but Gremorly doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the target drops to 0 HP, Gremorly ends it or Gremorly is turned or forced out by an effect like the Dispel Evil and Good spell. When the possession ends, Gremorly reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the target. The target is immune to this Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries.description: Reaction: When a creature that can see Honna's eyes starts its turn within Close range of Honna, Honna can force it to make a Strength Reaction Roll if Honna isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the creature is instantly petrified. Otherwise, a creature that fails the Reaction Roll begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the Reaction Roll at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see Honna until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at Honna in the meantime, it must immediately make the Reaction Roll. If Honna sees itself reflected on a polished surface within Close range of it and in an area of bright light, Honna is, due to its curse, affected by its own gaze.

One Small or Medium creature within Melee range that has the Incapacitated condition, is a Humanoid or Beast, and has 10 HP or fewer must make a Knowledge Reaction Roll. On a failure: The intellect devourer possesses the target, consumes its brain, and teleports inside its skull. While there, the intellect devourer has Total Cover against attacks and other effects originating outside its host. The intellect devourer retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; its understanding of Deep Speech; its telepathy; and its Detect Intelligence trait. It otherwise adopts the target's game statistics. It knows everything the target knew, including spells and languages. If the host body dies, the intellect devourer must leave it. The intellect devourer is also forced out if the target regains its devoured brain by means of a Wish spell. By spending Melee range of its movement, the intellect devourer can voluntarily leave the body, teleporting to the nearest unoccupied space within Melee range of it. The body then dies unless its brain is restored before the end of the intellect devourer's next turn.

entries.name: Swallow
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The eldritch horror makes one bite attack against a Medium or smaller target it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the target is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the eldritch horror, and it takes 6d6 magic damage (acid) at the start of each of the eldritch horror's turns. A eldritch horror can have only one creature swallowed at a time. If the eldritch horror takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the eldritch horror must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone (Vulnerable) in a space within Very Close range of the eldritch horror. If the eldritch horror dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using Close range of movement, exiting prone.

entries.name: Soul Binding
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 4d10+7 magic damage (necrotic). A creature reduced to 0 HP from this attack dies and has its soul imprisoned in one of the quori's eyes. The target can't be revived by any means short of a wish spell until the quori is destroyed.

entries.name: Mind Seed
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The quori touches one humanoid, which must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or be cursed. The curse lasts until it's removed by a remove curse or greater restoration spell. The cursed target suffers 1 level of exhaustion every 24 hours, and finishing a long rest doesn't reduce its exhaustion. If the cursed target reaches exhaustion level 6, it doesn't die; it instead becomes a thrall under the quori's control, and all its exhaustion is removed. Only the wish spell can free the thrall from this control.

entries.name: Swarm of Eyes
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The quori creates a swarm of spectral eyes that fills a sphere (Close range) centered on a point it can see within Far range of it. Each creature in that area must make an Instinct Reaction Roll. On a failure, a creature takes 10d8 magic damage (psychic), and it is blinded for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't blinded. A blinded creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that the quori can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by the quori; the quori then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. The quori now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. The quori can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, the quori ends it or the quori is forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, the quori reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to this quori's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

If the target is knocked prone (Vulnerable), the kamadan can make two attacks—one with its bite and one with its snakes—against it .

Additionally, any Medium or smaller Humanoid killed by the breath's damage, as well as every corpse of such a creature within the cone, becomes a zombie (see the Monster Manual) under Karavarix's control. The zombie acts on Karavarix's initiative but immediately after Karavarix's turn. Absent any other command, the zombie tries to kill any non-Undead creature it encounters.

entries.description: Passive: While in dim light or darkness, the dragon can become Hidden .

entries.description: Passive: While in sunlight, the dragon has disadvantage on attacks, as well as on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.

Each creature of the dragon's choice that is within Far range of the dragon and aware of it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or become frightened for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the dragon's Frightful Presence for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Breath Weapons
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The dragon uses one of the following breath weapons. Shadow Breath. The dragon exhales an icy blast in a cone (Far range). Each creature in that area must make a Strength Reaction Roll, taking 15d8 magic damage (necrotic) on a failure, or half as much damage on a successful one. A humanoid reduced to 0 HP by this damage dies, and an undead shadow rises from its corpse and acts immediately after the dragon in the initiative count. The shadow is under the dragon's control. Paralyzing Breath. The dragon exhales paralyzing gas in a cone (Far range). Each creature in that area must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be paralyzed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The dragon magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating no higher than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the dragon's choice). In a new form, the dragon retains its alignment, HP, Hit Dice, ability to speak, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as this action. Its statistics and capabilities are otherwise replaced by those of the new form, except any class features or legendary actions of that form.

entries.name: Wing Attack
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The dragon beats its wings. Each creature within Close range of the dragon must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take 2d6+10 physical damage and be knocked prone (Vulnerable). The dragon can then fly up to half its flying speed.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries.description: Passive: Kas can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

entries.name: Strength of the Night
entries.description: Passive: Kas doesn't require a coffin, and he drinks blood to sow terror rather than for sustenance. If destroyed, Kas revives in 1d100 nights in an unoccupied space in Tovag, his Domain of Dread. He can be permanently destroyed only by having a stake driven through his heart and then being beheaded. The stake must be cut from a tree growing in soil from Oerth, Kas's home world.

entries.name: Sunlight Hypersensitivity
entries.description: Passive: While in sunlight, Kas takes 20 radiant damage at the start of his turn, has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks, and can't use his Change Shape bonus action.

entries.name: Relentless (3)
entries.description: Passive: This adversary can be spotlighted up to 3 times per conflict. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

entries.description: Action: Make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 2d8+11 physical damage. The sword scores a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+8 physical damage plus 3d6 magic damage (necrotic). The target's HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and Kas regains a number of HP equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its HP maximum is reduced to 0. A Humanoid slain in this way and then buried rises the following night as a vampire spawn under Kas's control.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Kas transforms into a Medium cloud of mist. While in this form, Kas has a flying speed of Close range, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. While in mist form, Kas can pass through a space without squeezing as long as air can pass through that space, but he can't pass through water. Kas has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Strength Reaction Rolls, and he is immune to all non-magical damage except the damage he takes as part of his Vampire Weaknesses trait. While in mist form, Kas can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects.

entries.name: Menacing Glare
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Kas targets one creature he can see within Far range of himself. The target must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or have the frightened condition until the start of Kas's next turn.

entries.name: Rise, Fallen Soldier
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Kas magically summons a specter. The specter appears in an unoccupied space within Close range of Kas, whom it obeys. The specter takes its turn immediately after Kas. It lasts for 1 hour, until Kas dies, or until Kas dismisses it . Kas can't have more than two specters summoned at a time.

entries.name: Parrying Riposte
entries.description: Reaction: Kas adds 3 to his Difficulty against one melee attack that would hit him. He then makes one Vengeful Sword attack against the attacker if it is within his reach. On a hit, the target takes an additional 2d8 physical damage. Mark a Stress to use this reaction.

entries.name: Shapechanger
entries.description: Passive: If Kaylan isn't in sunlight or running water, it can use its action to polymorph into a Tiny bat or a Medium cloud of mist, or back into its true form. While in bat form, Kaylan can't speak, its walking speed is Melee range, and it has a flying speed of Close range. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are unchanged. Anything it is wearing transforms with it, but nothing it is carrying does. It reverts to its true form if it dies. While in mist form, Kaylan can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of Close range, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, and it can't pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Strength Reaction Rolls, and it is immune to all non-magical damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight.

entries.name: Legendary Resistance
entries.description: Reaction: When this adversary fails a Reaction Roll, you can spend a Fear to make it succeed instead.

entries.name: Misty Escape
entries.description: Reaction: When it drops to 0 HP outside its resting place, Kaylan transforms into a cloud of mist (as in the Shapechanger trait) instead of falling unconscious, provided that it isn't in sunlight or running water. If it can't transform, it is destroyed. While it has 0 HP in mist form, it can't revert to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in its resting place, it reverts to its vampire form. It is then paralyzed until it regains at least 1 HP. After spending 1 hour in its resting place with 0 HP, it regains 1 HP.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries.description: Passive: Kaylan regains 20 HP at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 HP and isn't in sunlight or running water. If Kaylan takes radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of Kaylan's next turn.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries.description: Passive: Kaylan can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

entries.name: Vampire Weaknesses
entries.description: Reaction: Kaylan has the following flaws:Forbiddance. Kaylan can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of the occupants. Harmed by Running Water. Kaylan takes 20 acid damage if it ends its turn in running water. Stake to the Heart. If a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into Kaylan's heart while Kaylan is incapacitated in its resting place, Kaylan is paralyzed until the stake is removed. Sunlight Hypersensitivity. Kaylan takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.

entries.name: Relentless (2)
entries.description: Passive: This adversary can be spotlighted up to 2 times per conflict. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

entries.name: Multiattack (Vampire Form Only)
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make 2 standard attacks, against one target or split between targets in range.

entries.name: Unarmed Strike (Vampire Form Only)
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d8+4 physical damage. Instead of dealing damage, Kaylan can grapple the target.

entries.name: Bite (Bat or Vampire Form Only)
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+4 physical damage plus 3d6 magic damage (necrotic). The target's HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and Kaylan regains HP equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0. A humanoid slain in this way and then buried in the ground rises the following night as a vampire spawn under Kaylan's control.

entries.name: Charm
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Kaylan targets one humanoid it can see within Close range of it. If the target can see Kaylan, the target must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll against this magic or be charmed by Kaylan. The charmed target regards Kaylan as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn't under Kaylan's control, it takes Kaylan's requests or actions in the most favorable way it can, and it is a willing target for Kaylan's bite attack. Each time Kaylan or Kaylan's companions do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the Reaction Roll, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until Kaylan is destroyed, is on a different plane of existence than the target, or takes its action to end the effect.

entries.name: Children of the Night
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Kaylan magically calls 2d4 swarms of bats or rats, provided that the sun isn't up. While outdoors, Kaylan can call 3d6 wolves instead. The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of Kaylan and obeying its spoken commands. The beasts remain for 1 hour, until Kaylan dies, or until Kaylan dismisses them .

entries.name: Unarmed Strike
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Kaylan makes one unarmed strike.

This benefit lasts until the end of the turn. If Kedjou expends a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the extra damage increases by 1d6 for each level above 1st.

A full keg robot can make one liquid attack per gallon before the liquid must be refilled. Filling a keg robot takes 2 rounds per gallon. Differing payloads can alter the keg robot's attacks from those presented here.

Each creature in the area must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be poisoned. While poisoned in this way, a creature has its speed halved by exposure to the potent brew. An affected creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Additionally, the beer shower extinguishes any fires or open flames in its area.

entries.name: Hot Oil Spray
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The keg robot sprays hot oil in a cone (Close range) or in a line (Close range) that is 5 feet wide. Each creature in the area must make an Agility Reaction Roll. On a failure, a creature takes 1d8+3 magic damage (fire) and falls prone (Vulnerable). On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage and doesn't fall prone (Vulnerable). Any creature affected by the hot oil spray that takes fire damage before the oil dries (after 1 minute) takes an additional 1d6 magic damage (fire), and the oil burns away. If the oil that remains in the area of the spray is lit, it burns for 1d4 rounds and deals 1d6 magic damage (fire) to any creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or ends its turn there.

entries.name: False Appearance

entries.name: Seaweed Shape
entries.description: Passive: The kelpie can use its action to reshape its body into the form of a humanoid or beast that is Small, Medium, or Large. Its statistics are otherwise unchanged. The disguise is convincing, unless the kelpie is in bright light or the viewer is within Close range of it, in which case the seams between the seaweed strands are visible. The kelpie returns to its true form if takes its action to do so or if it dies.

entries.name: Drowning Hypnosis
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The kelpie chooses one humanoid it can see within Very Far range of it. If the target can see the kelpie, the target must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be magically charmed while the kelpie maintains concentration, up to 10 minutes (as if concentrating on a spell). The charmed target is incapacitated, and instead of holding its breath underwater, it tries to breathe normally and immediately runs out of breath, unless it can breathe water. If the charmed target is more than Melee range away from the kelpie, the target must move on its turn toward the kelpie by the most direct route, trying to get within Melee range. It doesn't avoid opportunity attacks. Before moving into damaging terrain, such as lava or a pit, and whenever it takes damage from a source other than the kelpie or drowning, the target can repeat the Reaction Roll. A charmed target can also repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns. If the Reaction Roll is successful, the effect ends on it.A target that successfully saves is immune to this kelpie's hypnosis for the next 24 hours.

If it can't transform, it is destroyed. While it has 0 HP in mist form, it can't revert to its vampire form, and it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed. Once in its resting place, it reverts to its vampire form. It is then paralyzed until it regains at least 1 HP. After spending 1 hour in its resting place with 0 HP, it regains 1 HP.

If a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into Keresta's heart while Keresta is incapacitated in its resting place, Keresta is paralyzed until the stake is removed. Sunlight Hypersensitivity. Keresta takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.

entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d6+4 physical damage plus 3d6 magic damage (necrotic). The target's HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and Keresta regains HP equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its HP maximum to 0. A humanoid slain in this way and then buried in the ground rises the following night as a vampire spawn under Keresta's control.

entries.name: Charm
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Keresta targets one humanoid it can see within Close range of it. If the target can see Keresta, the target must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll against this magic or be charmed by Keresta. The charmed target regards Keresta as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn't under Keresta's control, it takes Keresta's requests or actions in the most favorable way it can, and it is a willing target for Keresta's bite attack. Each time Keresta or Keresta's companions do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the Reaction Roll, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until Keresta is destroyed, is on a different plane of existence than the target, or takes its action to end the effect.

entries.name: Children of the Night
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Keresta magically calls 2d4 swarms of bats or rats, provided that the sun isn't up. While outdoors, Keresta can call 3d6 giant centipedes instead. The called creatures arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of Keresta and obeying its spoken commands. The beasts remain for 1 hour, until Keresta dies, or until Keresta dismisses them .

Once the skunk has sprayed its musk, it can't do so again until it finishes a short or long rest.8: Wasp Nest in a Bag. entries.name: Regeneration
entries.description: Passive: The vampire regains 10 HP at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 HP and isn't in sunlight or running water. If the vampire takes radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Unusual Nature
entries.description: Passive: The vampire doesn't require air.

entries.name: Vampire Weaknesses
entries.description: Reaction: The vampire has the following flaws:Forbiddance. The vampire can't enter a residence without an invitation from one of the occupants. Harmed by Running Water. The vampire takes 20 acid damage when it starts its turn in running water. Stake to the Heart. The vampire is destroyed if a piercing weapon made of wood is driven into its heart while it is incapacitated in its resting place. Sunlight Hypersensitivity. The vampire takes 20 radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks.

entries.name: Bite
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Melee range. On a success, deal 1d4+4 physical damage plus 2d4 magic damage (necrotic). The target's HP maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains HP equal to that amount. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its HP maximum is reduced to 0.

The kolyarut moves up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks and can make one Unerring Blade attack against each creature it moves past. The kolyarut can cast the spell normally, or it can cast the spell on an unwilling creature it can see within Far range of itself. If it uses the latter option, the targeted creature must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be sent to a teleportation circle in the Hall of Concordance in Sigil.

entries.name: Etherealness
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Leedara enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. She is visible on the Material Plane while she is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet she can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

entries.name: Horrifying Visage
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Each non-undead creature within Far range of Leedara that can see her must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to Leedara's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that the ghost can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by Leedara; Leedara then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. Leedara now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. Leedara can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and she retains her alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. She otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, Leedara ends it or Leedara is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, Leedara reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to Leedara's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Leedara magically assumes the appearance she had in life, and her creature type changes to Humanoid, while retaining her other game statistics. This transformation ends if Leedara is reduced to 0 HP or uses an action to end it.

In a new form, Lhammaruntosz retains her alignment, HP, Hit Dice, ability to speak, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as this action. entries.name: Roleplaying Information
entries.description: A druid of the Emerald Enclave awakened the tree Lifferlas with a spell. Goldenfields is his home, its people his friends. Children like to carve their name and initials into his body and hang from his boughs, and he's happy with that. Ideal: "I exist to protect the people and plants of Goldenfields." Bond: "Children are wonderful. I would do anything to make them feel happy and safe." Flaw: "I can't remember people's names and often get them mixed up."

If no creature is near enough to move to and attack, the golem attacks an object, with preference for an object smaller than itself. Once the golem goes berserk, it continues to do so until it is destroyed or regains all its HP. The golem's creator, if within Far range of the berserk golem, can try to calm it by speaking firmly and persuasively. The golem must be able to hear its creator, who must take an action to make a Presence Roll (15). If the check succeeds, the golem ceases being berserk. If it takes damage while still at 40 HP or fewer, the golem might go berserk again.

entries.description: Passive: The living spell can enter another creature's space and vice versa, and it can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. The living spell can't detach from a solid surface, such as a wall, ceiling, or floor. If it has no surface to attach to, the living spell is destroyed (see "Planar Destruction" below).

entries.name: Extradimensional Chamber
entries.description: Reaction: When the living spell enters another creature's space (or vice versa) for the first time on a turn, the other creature must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or be pulled into the living spell's extradimensional space, an unfurnished stone chamber Close range in every dimension. A creature too big to fit in this space succeeds on the Reaction Roll automatically. Creatures in the chamber never run out of breathable air. Magic that enables transit between planes, such as plane shift, can be used to escape the chamber, which has no exits otherwise. Creatures trapped inside the extradimensional chamber can't see, target, or deal damage to the living spell; however, they can damage the room around them. Each Melee-square section of ceiling, wall, and floor in the chamber has Difficulty 17, 50 HP, immunity to poison and psychic damage, and immunity to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that is non-magical. If any section is reduced to 0 HP, the living spell and its chamber are destroyed (see "Planar Destruction" below).

entries.name: Magic Resistance

entries.name: Planar Destruction
entries.description: Reaction: The living spell is destroyed when it or a Melee-square section of its extradimensional chamber is reduced to 0 HP, or when the living spell has no surface to attach to. When the living spell is destroyed, the contents of its extradimensional chamber are expelled, appearing as close to the living spell's previous location as possible. Each expelled creature appears in a randomly determined unoccupied space, along with whatever it is wearing or carrying.

Anything it is wearing transforms with it, but nothing it is carrying does. It reverts to its true form if it dies. While in mist form, Lorry can't take any actions, speak, or manipulate objects. It is weightless, has a flying speed of Close range, can hover, and can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. In addition, if air can pass through a space, the mist can do so without squeezing, and it can't pass through water. It has advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Strength Reaction Rolls, and it is immune to all non-magical damage, except the damage it takes from sunlight.

Once in its resting place, it reverts to its vampire form. It is then paralyzed until it regains at least 1 HP. After spending 1 hour in its resting place with 0 HP, it regains 1 HP.

Each time Lorry or Lorry's companions do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the Reaction Roll, ending the effect on itself on a success. entries.name: Bite

entries.name: Cold Breath
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The dragon exhales a blast of frost in a cone (Close range). Each creature in the cone must make a Strength Reaction Roll. On a failure, the creature takes 3d8 magic damage (cold), and its speed is halved until the end of its next turn. On a successful Reaction Roll, the creature takes half as much damage, and its speed isn't reduced.

Both trees must be large or bigger.

entries.name: Fey Charm
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Lungtian targets one humanoid or beast that she can see within Close range of her. If the target can see Lungtian, it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be magically charmed. The charmed creature regards Lungtian as a trusted friend to be heeded and protected. Although the target isn't under Lungtian's control, it takes Lungtian's requests or actions in the most favorable way it can. Each time Lungtian or its allies do anything harmful to the target, it can repeat the Reaction Roll, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, the effect lasts 24 hours or until Lungtian dies, is on a different plane of existence from the target, or ends the effect . If a target's Reaction Roll is successful, the target is immune to Lungtian's Fey Charm for the next 24 hours. Lungtian can have no more than one humanoid and up to three beasts charmed at a time.

entries.name: Night Hag Items
entries.description: Reaction: A night hag carries two very rare magic items that she must craft for herself. If either object is lost, the night hag will go to great lengths to retrieve it, as creating a new tool takes time and effort. Heartstone: This lustrous black gem allows a night hag to become ethereal while it is in her possession. The touch of a heartstone also cures any disease. Crafting a heartstone takes 30 days. Soul Bag: When an evil humanoid dies as a result of a night hag's Nightmare Haunting, Maggie catches the soul in this black sack made of stitched flesh. A soul bag can hold only one evil soul at a time, and only the night hag who crafted the bag can catch a soul with it. Crafting a soul bag takes 7 days and a humanoid sacrifice (whose flesh is used to make the bag).

entries.name: Change Shape
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Maggie magically polymorphs into a Small or Medium female humanoid, or back into her true form. Her statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. She reverts to her true form if she dies.

entries.name: Etherealness
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Maggie magically enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. To do so, Maggie must have a heartstone in her possession.

entries.name: Nightmare Haunting
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. While on the Ethereal Plane, Maggie magically touches a sleeping humanoid on the Material Plane. A protection from evil and good spell cast on the target prevents this contact, as does a magic circle. As long as the contact persists, the target has dreadful visions. If these visions last for at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from its rest, and its HP maximum is reduced by 1d10. If this effect reduces the target's HP maximum to 0, the target dies, and if the target was evil, its soul is trapped in Maggie's soul bag. The reduction to the target's HP maximum lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to make an attack against a target within Very Close range. On a success, deal 4d8+4 physical damage. The target is Restrained. Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the hunter can't make a Tail attack against another target.

entries.name: Mage Tracker (Sentry Form Only)
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The hunter emits a pulse of energy that helps it better locate its magical quarry. Each creature within Far range of the hunter that has the ability to cast spells must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be mystically marked by the hunter for 1 hour. While marked, a creature can't become hidden from the hunter and gains no benefit from the invisible condition against the hunter. Additionally, while a marked creature is on the same plane of existence as the hunter, the hunter always knows the distance and direction to the creature.

entries.name: Shift Form
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The hunter folds into its drone-like sentry form or unfolds into its hunter form. Its game statistics are the same in each form.

entries.name: Consume and Destroy
entries.description: Reaction: When the hunter takes damage from a spell, it takes only half the triggering damage (rounded down). If the creature that cast the spell is within Far range of the hunter, that creature must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take the other half of the damage. Mark a Stress to use this reaction.

entries.name: Limited Magic Immunity

The curse takes effect whenever the target takes a short or long rest, filling the target's thoughts with horrible images and dreams. The cursed target gains no benefit from finishing a short or long rest. The curse lasts until it is lifted by a remove curse spell or similar magic.

entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. Mahadi summons Ilzabet, an erinyes bound to him by an infernal contract. The erinyes appears in an unoccupied space within Far range of him, acts as his ally, and can't summon other devils. The erinyes remains for 10 minutes or until Mahadi dismisses it as an action. If the erinyes dies, Mahadi loses this action option.

Its statistics are the same in each form, except for the speed changes noted. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

The vortex is a cylinder (Close range) centered on that point. Each creature other than Malaxxix in that area must make an Agility Reaction Roll. On a failure, a creature takes 10d6 magic damage and has the restrained condition while within the cylinder. On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage and is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space outside the cylinder. The vortex lasts until the start of Malaxxix's next turn.

An affected target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

While trapped in this way, the target is blinded and restrained, has total cover from an attacks and other effects outside the mantrap, and takes at the start of each of the target's turns. If the mantrap dies, the creature inside it is no longer restrained by it. A mantrap can engulf only one creature at a time.

entries.name: Etherealness
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Marisa enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

entries.name: Horrifying Visage
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Each non-undead creature within Far range of Marisa that can see it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that Marisa can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by Marisa; Marisa then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. Marisa now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. Marisa can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, Marisa ends it or Marisa is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, Marisa reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Roleplaying Information
entries.description: Sheriff Markham of Bryn Shander is a brawny, likable man of few words. Nothing is more important to him than protecting Icewind Dale. He judges others by their actions, not their words. Ideal: "All people deserve to be treated with dignity." Bond: "Duvessa is a natural leader, but she needs help. That's my job." Flaw: "I bury my emotions and have no interest in small talk."

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries.description: Reaction: When a creature that can see Marlos's eyes starts its turn within Close range of him, Marlos can force it to make a Strength Reaction Roll if Marlos isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the creature is instantly petrified. Otherwise, a creature that fails the Reaction Roll begins to turn to stone and is restrained. The restrained creature must repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of its next turn, becoming petrified on a failure or ending the effect on a success. The petrification lasts until the creature is freed by the greater restoration spell or other magic. Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the Reaction Roll at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see Marlos until the start of its next turn, when it can decide to avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at Marlos in the meantime, it must immediately make the Reaction Roll. If Marlos sees himself reflected on a polished surface within Close range of him and in an area of bright light, Marlos is, due to his curse, affected by his own gaze.

Constructs, Oozes, Plants, and Undead succeed on the Reaction Roll automatically. On a failure, the target takes 2d4 magic damage (psychic) and becomes memory drained until it finishes a long rest or the memory web is destroyed. While memory drained, the target must roll a d4 each time it makes an ability check or attack, subtracting the d4 roll from it. Each time the target is memory drained beyond the first, the die size increases by one: the d4 becomes a d6, the d6 becomes a d8, and so on until the die becomes a d20, at which point the target has the unconscious condition for 1 hour. If a memory drained creature is the target of the Greater Restoration or Heal spell, the memory drained effect ends on it. On a successful Reaction Roll, the target takes half as much damage only.

entries.name: Horrifying Visage
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Each non-undead creature within Far range of Meri that can see it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If a target's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed with a greater restoration spell, but only within 24 hours of it occurring.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that Meri can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by Meri; Meri then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. Meri now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. Meri can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, Meri ends it or Meri is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, Meri reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Unleash Void
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. The mind flayer opens a rift into the Far Realm, centered on a point the mind flayer can see within Far range of itself, and a tentacle lashes across creatures near the rift. Each creature other than mind flayers within Close range of the rift must make a Knowledge Reaction Roll, after which the tentacle disappears and the rift closes. On a failure, a creature takes 4d8 magic damage (cold) from the rift plus 4d8 magic damage (psychic) from the tentacle and has the stunned condition for 1 minute. On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage only. A stunned creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Warp Reality
entries.description: Reaction: When hit by an attack, the mind flayer gains a +4 bonus to its Difficulty against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. Then the mind flayer, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, magically teleports up to Far range to an unoccupied space it can see. Mark a Stress to use this reaction.

entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The matter smith magically manipulates the energy of the plane of existence it's on to produce one of the following effects (choose one or roll a d4):1-2: Chains. The matter smith creates spectral bindings around a creature it can see within Close range of itself. The target must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or have the restrained condition until the end of its next turn.3-4: Magic Shield. The matter smith conjures a floating, spectral shield that grants the matter smith a +5 bonus to its Difficulty until the shield disappears at the start of the matter smith's next turn. The first time a creature misses a melee attack against the matter smith while the shield is conjured, that creature takes 2d6 magic damage.

entries.name: Eye Ray
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. The mindwitness shoots one magical eye ray at random (roll a d6, and reroll if the ray has already been used this turn), choosing one target it can see within Far range of it:1: Aversion Ray. The targeted creature must make a Presence Reaction Roll. On a failure, the target has disadvantage on attacks for 1 minute. The target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.2: Fear Ray. The targeted creature must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. The target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.3: Psychic Ray. The target must succeed on a Knowledge Reaction Roll or take 6d8 magic damage (psychic).4: Slowing Ray. The targeted creature must make an Agility Reaction Roll. On a failure, the target's speed is halved for 1 minute. In addition, the creature can't take reactions, and it can take either an action or its action on its turn but not both. The creature can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.5: Stunning Ray. The targeted creature must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or be stunned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.6: Telekinetic Ray. If the target is a creature, it must make a Strength Reaction Roll. On a failure, the mindwitness moves it up to Close range in any direction, and it is restrained by the ray's telekinetic grip until the start of the mindwitness's next turn or until the mindwitness is incapacitated. If the target is an object weighing 300 pounds or less that isn't being worn or carried, it is telekinetically moved up to Close range in any direction. The mindwitness can also exert fine control on objects with this ray, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a door or a container.

While enlarged, the minotaur is Large, doubles its damage dice on Strength-based weapon attacks (included in the attacks), and makes Strength checks and Strength Reaction Rolls with advantage. If the minotaur lacks the room to become Large, the minotaur doesn't change size.

For the next hour, the minotaur knows the current distance and direction to the target if it is on the same plane of existence. The link ends if the minotaur has the incapacitated condition or uses this ability on a different target.

entries.name: Roleplaying Information
entries.description: Innkeeper Miros is a retired carnival attraction, dubbed "the Yeti" because of his barrel-shaped body and the thick, white hair covering his arms, chest, back, and head. When Goldenfields suffers, so does his business, so he takes strides to protect the compound. Ideal: "As does the Emerald Enclave, I believe that civilization and the wilderness need to learn to coexist." Bond: "Make fun of me all you like, but don't speak ill of my inn or my employees." Flaw: "When something upsets me, I have a tendency to fly into a rage."

Heartstone: This lustrous black gem allows a night hag to become ethereal while it is in her possession. The touch of a heartstone also cures any disease. Crafting a heartstone takes 30 days. Soul Bag: When an evil humanoid dies as a result of a night hag's Nightmare Haunting, Morgantha catches the soul in this black sack made of stitched flesh. A soul bag can hold only one evil soul at a time, and only the night hag who crafted the bag can catch a soul with it. Crafting a soul bag takes 7 days and a humanoid sacrifice (whose flesh is used to make the bag).

If these visions last for at least 1 hour, the target gains no benefit from its rest, and its HP maximum is reduced by 1d10. If this effect reduces the target's HP maximum to 0, the target dies, and if the target was evil, its soul is trapped in Morgantha's soul bag. The reduction to the target's HP maximum lasts until removed by the greater restoration spell or similar magic.

That creature then hears Nafas's last wish: for the creature to take his place. If the creature accepts, it is transformed into a noble djinni. The creature's game statistics are replaced by those of Nafas (including this trait), though it retains its name, alignment, and personality. The creature also inherits Nafas's palace and all it contains. If the creature refuses, Nafas gains a new body in 1d10 days, regaining all his HP and appearing in a random safe location on the Infinite Staircase.

The vortex lasts as long as Nafas maintains concentration (as if concentrating on a spell). When the vortex appears, each creature other than Nafas in the vortex's area must make a Strength Reaction Roll. On a failure, a creature takes 8d8 magic damage and has the restrained condition. On a successful Reaction Roll, a creature takes half as much damage only and moves to the nearest unoccupied space outside the vortex. On subsequent turns, Nafas can use this action to move the vortex up to Far range. When the vortex enters a creature's space for the first time on a turn, the creature must make the same Reaction Roll as when the vortex first appeared. Creatures restrained by the vortex move with it.A creature restrained by the vortex, or another creature that can reach it, can use its action to make a Strength Roll (22). On a successful check, the restrained creature is no longer restrained and moves to the nearest unoccupied space outside the vortex.

The illusion ends if Pu'pu takes its action to end it or if she dies. The changes wrought by this effect fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, Pu'pu could appear to have smooth skin, but someone touching her would feel her rough flesh. Otherwise, a creature must take an action to visually inspect the illusion and succeed on a Knowledge Roll (20) to discern that Pu'pu is disguised.

entries.name: Roleplaying Information
entries.description: Narth sells gear to adventurers, and he also has an adventurous spirit. The Lionshield Coster pays him well, but he longs to make a name for himself. At the same time, he runs a business with his partner Alaestra and knows she wouldn't forgive him if he ran off and never returned. Ideal: "The bigger the risk, the greater the reward." Bond: "I adore my colleague Alestra, and I'd like to do something to impress her." Flaw: "I'll risk life and limb to become a legend.-"

entries.name: Horrifying Visage
entries.description: Action: Mark a Stress to use this ability. Each non-undead creature within Far range of the ghost that can see it must succeed on an Instinct Reaction Roll or be frightened for 1 minute. If the Reaction Roll fails by 5 or more, the target also ages 1d4 × 10 years. A frightened target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. If the target's Reaction Roll is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Horrifying Visage for the next 24 hours. The aging effect can be reversed by a greater restoration spell, but only if it is cast within 24 hours.

entries.name: Possession
entries.description: Action: Spend a Fear to use this ability. One humanoid that the ghost can see within Melee range of it must succeed on a Presence Reaction Roll or be possessed by the ghost; the ghost then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. The ghost now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. The ghost can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies. The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 HP, the ghost ends it or the ghost is turned or forced out by an effect like the dispel evil and good spell. When the possession ends, the ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within Melee range of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the Reaction Roll or after the possession ends.

entries.name: Roleplaying Information
entries.description: Goldenfields' crops are vital Waterdeep's survival, which is why the Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors sent Naxene to make sure the temple-farm is adequately defended. At first she regarded the task as a punishment, but now she appreciates the peace and quiet. Ideal: "There's no problem that can't be solved with magic." Bond: "I have great respect for Lady Laeral Silverhand of Waterdeep. She and the Lords' Alliance are going to bring some much-needed order to this lawless land." Flaw: "I'm too smart to be wrong about anything."

While attached, the necrichor takes only half damage dealt to it (round down), and the target takes the remaining damage. The necrichor can attach to only one creature at a time. The attached necrichor can telepathically control the target's move, action, or both. When controlled this way, the target can take only the Attack action (necrichor chooses the target) or the Dash action. The attached target can repeat the Reaction Roll at the end of each of its turns, detaching from the necrichor and forcing it to move into the nearest unoccupied space on a success.
